messages.subject: Re: possible burrow parameter bug?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adam,

What's happening is that your animal is starting off as an egg via the DEB model, at a depth of 10cm (set by parameter 'soilnode' which by default is set to node 4 = 10 cm). With the parameters you've provided, it never hatches. If you e.g. make the threshold maturity level for hatching, E_Hb, half the value of that in your example, it will hatch and then stay on the surface as you expected. There is probably something awry with your DEB model parameters. Also, note that you haven't specified E_0, the initial energy content of the egg, so it's defaulting to that of the water skink. You need to provide an estimate of this for your species.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Organism Temp Question
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

This is a very dumb question that I didn't realize was an issue until just now.  When the Usrhyt is specified does that mean the model is essentially assuming the organism is floating in the air at that height?  Or are substrate temps included? Essentially looking at the Kearney and Porter 2016 paper the air temp at 1 cm is 10 degrees or more lower than the soil or rock substrates.  So in the model are animals touching the substrate/can they or is it just using the air temp at 1 cm?

Mike

Martin

messages.subject: Re: possible burrow parameter bug?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adam - you also need to set the initial DEB state variables to that of an adult - that's what the commented-out code in your example is doing:

# V_init <- L.p^3
# E_init <- E.m
# E_H_init <- E.Hp+2

which then needs to be passed to the ectotherm function. Try the example below to see what should happen forthe default animal, the eastern water skink, with all default settings except for making them oviparous and preventing them from burrowing. The code pulls out the required starting conditions from the allstat file (which you can get from https://www.bio.vu.nl/thb/deb/deblab/add_my_pet/species_list.html under the the 'Collection' dropdown).

I did notice a little bug when putting this example together in that the first hour starts off at -10 cm, which is fixed by making soilnode = 1. For some reason it is behaving as an egg in the first hour. I'll look into this.

library(NicheMapR)
library(R.matlab)
#allStat<-readMat('allStat.mat') # this will take a few minutes
#save(allStat, file = 'allstat.Rda') # save it as an R data file for faster future loading
load('c:/git/AmPtool/allStat.Rda')
species <- "Eulamprus.quoyii" # must be in the AmP collection - see allDEB.species list
allDEB.species <- unlist(labels(allStat$allStat))
species.slot <- which(allDEB.species == species) # find the slot with the species of interest
par.names <- unlist(labels(allStat$allStat[[species.slot]])) # get parameter names
for(i in 1:length(par.names)){ # pull parameters into memory
  assign(par.names[i], unlist(allStat$allStat[[species.slot]][i]))
}
micro <- micro_global(loc = c(144.5, -16), timeinterval = 365)
ecto <- ectotherm(DEB = 1, viviparous = 0, V_init = L.p ^ 3, E_H_init = E.Hp, E_init = E.m, burrow = 0, soilnode = 1)
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$DEP, type = 'l')

All the best,
Mike
